rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two ends of the day are morning and evening: dawn is the morning prayer, noon and afternoon are the evening prayers, and the night intervals are sunset and night prayers.
rows.anchor: وصلاة الغدوة : الفجر ، وصلاة العشية : الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative of the two ends is adverbial because the words are annexed to times; the annexed term takes the syntactic status of its complement.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب طرفي النهار على الظرف ، لأنهما مضافان إلى الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He records forms with damma, quiescent lām, and the form zu lfā; the last means a near interval of night, as does qurbā.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وزلفا ) ، بضمتين . وزلفا ، بسكون اللام . وزلفى : بوزن قربى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On another parsing, the night intervals are prayers by which one draws near to God, so the phrase coordinates with prayer.
rows.anchor: وحقها على هذا التفسير أن تعطف على الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that acts of obedience expiate minor sins.
rows.anchor: أن يراد تكفير الصغائر بالطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says one prayer expiates what lies between it and the next, provided major sins are avoided.
rows.anchor: إن الصلاة إلى الصلاة كفارة ما بينهما ما اجتنبت الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation is that good deeds act as a moral prompting that helps people leave sins; he links this to reciting scripture.
rows.anchor: إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات ، بأن يكن لطفا في تركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is reported to have followed the repentance of Abu al-Yusr ʿAmr ibn Ghaziyya after he embraced and kissed a woman, then confessed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي اليسر عمرو بن غزية الأنصاري ، كان يبيع التمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abu Bakr and ʿUmar each advised the penitent to conceal the matter and repent; when ʿUmar asked whether the verse applied only to him, the Prophet said it was for everyone.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر : أهذا له خاصة أم للناس عامة ؟ فقال : بل للناس عامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another prophetic report instructs him to perform ablution well and pray two rakʿas, then cites the verse about good deeds removing sins.
rows.anchor: توضأ وضوءا حسنا وصل ركعتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers to the command to remain upright and what follows it; this is an admonition for those who take admonition.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى قوله { فاستقم } فما بعده { ذكرى للذكرين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has al-sijn with fatḥ, treating it as a verbal noun; the women collectively urged and adorned compliance while warning him against prison and humiliation.
rows.anchor: وقال { يدعوننى } على إسناد الدعوة إليهن جميعا ، لأنهن تنصحن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf prefers prison to sin because he weighs patient endurance for God, the ugliness of disobedience, and each act's outcome, rather than bodily pleasure and discomfort.
rows.anchor: نظرا في حسن الصبر على احتمالها لوجه الله ، وفي قبح المعصية ، وفي عاقبة كل واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His plea to be turned away from their guile seeks God's subtle help and protection, as prophets and righteous people do while resolving to be patient; it does not ask God to compel chastity.
rows.anchor: فزع منه إلى ألطاف الله وعصمته ، كعادة الأنبياء والصالحين فيما عزم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣbu means to incline toward them, with ṣabwah denoting desire; the east wind is called ṣabā because souls incline to its pleasant breeze.
rows.anchor: أمل إليهن . والصبوة : الميل إلى الهوى . ومنها : الصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading derives aṣbu from ṣabābah, passionate yearning.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( أصب إليهن ) من الصبابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among the ignorant may mean failing to act on what one knows, which makes one like the ignorant, or being foolish, since a wise person does not do wrong.
rows.anchor: من الذين لا يعملون بما يعلمون . لأن من لا جدوى لعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response is mentioned although no prior explicit prayer appears because the conditional request to avert their guile itself carries a plea for protection.
rows.anchor: لأن قوله { وإلا تصرف عنى } فيه معنى طلب الصرف والدعاء باللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Hearer of those who seek refuge in Him and Knower of their conditions and what benefits them.
rows.anchor: { السميع } لدعوات الملتجئين إليه { العليم } بأحوالهم وما يصلحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implicit subject of bada is a newly formed opinion, namely their decision to imprison Yusuf; the pronoun refers to the Aziz and his household.
rows.anchor: فاعله مضمر ، لدلالة ما يفسره عليه وهو : ليسجننه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs were evidence of Yusuf's innocence; the wife nevertheless persuaded and controlled her compliant husband, who followed her plan to imprison and humiliate him.
rows.anchor: وما كان ذلك إلا باستنزال المرأة لزوجها ، وفتلها منه في الذروة والغارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife either gave up hope that Yusuf would obey her or hoped prison would humble him and make him compliant.
rows.anchor: وذلك لما أيست من طاعته لها ، أو لطمعها في أن يذلله السجن ويسخره لها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan's reading latasjunannahu addresses the Aziz and those around him, or addresses the Aziz alone deferentially.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة الحسن : ( لتسجننه ) بالتاء على الخطاب : خاطب به بعضهم العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥattā ḥīn means for a period, apparently the duration the wife proposed while waiting to see what Yusuf would do.
rows.anchor: حتى حين } إلى زمان ، كأنها اقترحت أن يسجن زمانا حتى تبصر ما يكون منه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud's reading ʿattā ḥīn is a Hudhayl dialect form.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود ( عتى حين ) وهي لغة هذيل ، وعن عمر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: After hearing a man recite ʿattā ḥīn, ʿUmar asked his teacher and wrote Ibn Masʿud to teach Quraysh speech rather than Hudhayl speech.
rows.anchor: فكتب إليه : إن الله أنزل هذا القرآن فجعله عربيا وأنزله بلغة قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿa marks companionship being newly entered into, so the two youths entered prison in Yusuf's company.
rows.anchor: يدل على معنى الصحبة واستحداثها ، تقول : خرجت مع الأمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths were the king's baker and cupbearer, imprisoned on suspicion that they were poisoning him when Yusuf was admitted.
rows.anchor: { فتيان } عبدان للملك : خبازه وشرابيه : رقي إليه أنهما يسمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statements describe past dreams; khamr names grapes by what they become, and in the language of Oman it means grapes directly.
rows.anchor: { إنى أرانى } يعني في المنام ، وهي حكاية حال ماضية { أعصر خمرا } يعني عنبا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads ʿinaban, grapes, in place of khamran.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود ( أعصر عنبا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥsinīn may mean skilled interpreters of dreams, learned men, or people who treat fellow prisoners well.
rows.anchor: { من المحسنين } من الذين يحسنون عبارة الرؤيا ، أي : يجيدونها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports that Yusuf comforted despondent prisoners, urging them to be patient and promising reward; they praised his character and asked who he was.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : كان في السجن ناس قد انقطع رجاؤهم وطال حزنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prison report says Yusuf identified himself through his lineage: son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham, and the guard promised him good treatment despite being unable to free him.
rows.anchor: أنا يوسف ابن صفي الله يعقوب ابن ذبيح الله إسحاق ابن خليل الله إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf asked the two men not to love him, saying that love had brought him calamity through his aunt, father, and the Aziz's wife.
rows.anchor: أنشدكما بالله أن لا تحباني ، فوالله ما أحبني أحد قط إلا دخل علي من حبه بلاء

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the two men feigned dreams to test Yusuf: the cupbearer dreamed of three grape clusters pressed for the king, while the baker dreamed of three food baskets attacked by birds.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي أنهما تحالما له ليمتحناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in nabbiʾnā bi-taʾwīlihi refers to the story they recounted and functions like a demonstrative pronoun.
rows.anchor: والضمير يجري مجرى اسم الإشارة في نحوه كأنه قيل : نبئنا بتأويل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who will serve wine is the cupbearer; one reading has him give his lord a drink, while ʿIkrima's reading uses a passive construction.
rows.anchor: يريد الشرابي { فيسقى ربه } سيده

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima reads yusqā rabbahu, with the passive meaning that he will be given drink to satisfy him.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة ( فيسقي ربه ) أي يسقي ما يروي به على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf interprets the cupbearer's vine as the king and his good standing, with three days in prison before release; the baker's three baskets mean three days before execution.
rows.anchor: ثم تخرج وتعود إلى ما كنت عليه ، وقال للثاني : ما رأيت من السلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the men asked about different dreams, al-amr means their shared accusation of poisoning and the outcome of their imprisonment: one would escape and one die.
rows.anchor: المراد بالأمر ما اتهما به من سم الملك وما سجنا من أجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the men had fabricated the dreams to test Yusuf; he told them the outcome would occur whether they had spoken truthfully or lied.
rows.anchor: وقيل : جحدا وقالا : ما رأينا شيئا ، على ما روي أنهما تحالما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Yusuf interpreted by reasoning, he was the one who thought the cupbearer would be saved; if he interpreted by revelation, the cupbearer was the one who knew with certainty.
rows.anchor: الظان هو يوسف إن كان تأويله بطريق الاجتهاد ، وإن كان بطريق الوحي فالظان هو الشرابي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf asked the cupbearer to describe his case to the king in hopes the king would rescue him.
rows.anchor: صفني عند الملك بصفتي ، وقص عليه قصتي لعله يرحمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Satan caused the cupbearer to forget to mention Yusuf to his master; an alternative says Yusuf forgot God when he entrusted his case to someone else.
rows.anchor: فأنسى الشرابي { ذكر ربه } أن يذكره لربه . وقيل فأنسي يوسف ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buḍʿ means three to nine years; most reports say Yusuf remained imprisoned seven years.
rows.anchor: البضع ما بين الثلاث إلى التسع ، وأكثر الأقاويل على أنه لبث فيه سبع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan can prompt forgetfulness by distracting a person, but initiating forgetfulness directly is within God's power alone; the verse links this to abrogation.
rows.anchor: وأما الإنساء ابتداء فلا يقدر عليه إلا الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive in dhikri rabbihi is licensed by close association with the king, or by ellipsis of the word reports before lord.
rows.anchor: لأن الإضافة تكون بأدنى ملابسة . أو على تقدير : فأنساه الشيطان ذكر أخبار ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking another person's help is generally permissible, supported by verses and reports, including God's help for servants who help one another and relief of a believer's distress.
rows.anchor: الله في عون العبد ما دام العبد في عون أخيه المسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though help may be sought even from non-Muslims to repel harm, a prophet's better course is to entrust a trial only to God, especially to avoid unbelievers gloating.
rows.anchor: والأحسن والأولى بالنبي أن لا يكل أمره إذا ابتلي ببلاء إلا إلى ربه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan would weep at this verse and say that when trouble comes, people like us turn to other people.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه كان يبكي إذا قرأها ويقول : نحن إذا نزل بنا أمر فزعنا إلى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Yusuf's release neared, Egypt's king Rayyan ibn al-Walid saw seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven ripe green ears overcome by seven dry ears, but found no interpreter.
rows.anchor: لما دنا فرج يوسف ، رأى ملك مصر ( الريان بن الوليد ) رؤيا عجيبة هالته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making fat an adjective of cows distinguishes the seven by a type of cow, whereas making it describe seven would distinguish by genus before adding the quality.
rows.anchor: قلت : إذا أوقعتها صفة لبقرات . فقد قصدت إلى أن تميز السبع بنوع من البقرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ʿijāf cannot alone specify a count's genus; substantivized adjectives such as horsemen or companions can serve as classifiers, unlike mere adjectives.
rows.anchor: والعجاف وصف لا يقع البيان به وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dry ears are also seven: the context's count governs cows and green ears, and the word ukhar means seven others.
rows.anchor: فوجب أن يتناول معنى الأخر السبع ، ويكون قوله : { وأخر يابسات } بمعنى وسبعا أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coordinating dry ears as a genitive adjective of the green ears would conflict with ukhar, which requires them to be other than the seven.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الأخر يقتضي أن تكون غير السبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressed council comprises leading scholars and sages.
rows.anchor: كأنه أراد الأعيان من العلماء والحكماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lam in lil-ruʾyā may explain the object, compensate when an object precedes its verb, mark competence as a predicate, or accompany an understood verb of volunteering.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله { للرؤيا } إما أن تكون للبيان ، كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basic sense of interpreting a dream is to state its end or outcome, like crossing a river to reach its far side; taʾwīl likewise names its destination.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة ( عبرت الرؤيا ) ذكرت عاقبتها وآخر أمرها ، كما تقول : عبرت النهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light form ʿabartu is the form trusted authorities use; he says they reject the doubled form, taʿbīr, and muʿabbir.
rows.anchor: وعبرت الرؤيا بالتخفيف ، هو الذي اعتمده الأثبات ، ورأيتهم ينكرون ( عبرت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazraʿūna is formally a report but functions as a command, intensifying the obligation by presenting the ordered action as certain to occur.
rows.anchor: خبر في معنى الأمر ، كقوله : { تؤمنون بالله ورسوله وتجاهدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾban may have a still or vowelled hamza; it is a verbal noun used adverbially or as a circumstantial description of the people working diligently.
rows.anchor: بسكون الهمزة وتحريكها ، وهما مصدر : دأب في العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping grain in its husk protects it from pests.
rows.anchor: لئلا يتسوس . و { يأكلن } من الإسناد المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The years are made the grammatical subjects of eating by figurative attribution, while their people are the actual eaters; yuḥṣinūn means you preserve and store.
rows.anchor: و { يأكلن } من الإسناد المجازي : جعل أكل أهلهن مسندا إليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuʿṣirūn can mean people press grapes, olives, or sesame, or milk livestock; a passive reading means they are rescued, and an active sense means they rescue themselves.
rows.anchor: يعصرون } بالياء والتاء : يعصرون العنب والزيتون والسمسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuʿṣirūn may instead mean that they receive rain, with either a verb meaning rain or an omitted preposition understood.
rows.anchor: وقيل { يعصرون } يمطرون ، من أعصرت السحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fat cows and green ears represent seven fertile years; the lean cows and dry ears represent seven famine years, followed by a blessed, abundant eighth year known through revelation.
rows.anchor: تأول البقرات السمان والسنبلات الخضر بسنين مخاصيب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says God gave Yusuf knowledge of a further year.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة : زاده الله علم سنة . فإن قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The end of a famine implies some fertility in general, but the detailed promise that people will receive relief and press produce in that year can only be known by revelation.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فيه يغاث الناس وفيه يعصرون } تفصيل لحال العام ، وذلك لا يعلم إلا بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf delays answering the king until the women's role is investigated, clearing his name so rivals cannot use his long imprisonment to lower his standing.
rows.anchor: وقدم سؤال النسوة ليظهر براءة ساحته عما قرف به وسجن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode supports a duty to avoid suspicion and the places that give rise to it; a prophetic report warns believers not to stand in places of accusation.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن الاجتهاد في نفي التهم واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic example has Muḥammad identify the woman accompanying him at night to passersby, preventing suspicion.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم للمارين به في معتكفه وعنده بعض نسائه ( هي فلانة ) اتقاء للتهمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report marvels at Yusuf's patience: the Prophet says he would have conditioned his interpretation on release and, after so long, would have hurried out when summoned.
rows.anchor: لقد عجبت من يوسف وكرمه وصبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf asks the king to inquire about the women's affair because a question will prompt a thorough search and expose the story clearly.
rows.anchor: لأن السؤال مما يهيج الإنسان ويحركه للبحث عما سئل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf's graciousness and good manners appear in sparing the Aziz's wife from mention and referring only to the women who cut their hands.
rows.anchor: ومن كرمه وحسن أدبه : أنه لم يذكر سيدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inna rabbī means God; His knowledge of their plot may describe its depth, witness to their plotting and Yusuf's innocence, or threaten requital.
rows.anchor: { إن ربى } إن الله تعالى : { بكيدهن عليم } أراد أنه كيد عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā khaṭbukun means what is your affair; Yusuf asks whether the women found any inclination toward them in him.
rows.anchor: { ما خطبكن } ما شأنكن { إذ راودتن يوسف } هل وجدتن منه ميلا إليكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women say ḥāsha li-llāh to express amazement at Yusuf's chastity, self-respect, and freedom from suspicion.
rows.anchor: تعجبا من عفته وذهابه بنفسه عن شيء من الريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive reading ḥuḥṣiṣa means the truth became established; its form is associated with a camel settling onto its chest.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( حصحص ) على البناء للمفعول ، وهو من حصحص البعير إذا ألقى ثفناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question a-innaka is read interrogatively or affirmatively; Ubayy's reading adds aw anta Yusuf, with the first alternative elided, conveying repeated astonishment.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( أئنك ) على الاستفهام . وأنك ، على الإيجاب وفي قراءة أبي : ( أئنك أو أنت يوسف ) ، على معنى أئنك يوسف أو أنت يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They recognized Yusuf from his appearance and manner of speech, or from his pearl-like teeth when he smiled, or a mark shared with Jacob and Sarah.
rows.anchor: رأوا في روائه وشمائله حين كلمهم بذلك ما شعروا به أنه هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusuf mentions his brother because that detail explains who he is in answer to their question, even though they already knew his brother.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان في ذكر أخيه بيان لما سألوه عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yattaqi means fear God's punishment, while yasbir means refrain from sins and persist in obedience; muḥsinīn replaces a pronoun because it includes both qualities.
rows.anchor: { من يتق } من يخف الله وعقابه { ويصبر } عن المعاصي وعلى الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers confess they deliberately sinned, lacked piety and patience, and were humbled while God raised Yusuf through his virtue.
rows.anchor: وإن شأننا وحالنا أنا كنا خاطئين متعمدين للإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tharīb means reproach; its root evokes removing the fatty covering of the stomach, a metaphor for stripping dignity by rebuke.
rows.anchor: وأصل التثريب من الثرب وهو الشحم الذي هو غاشية الكرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Today may attach to no reproach, to the understood phrase upon you, or to forgiveness; alternatively today God forgives them as a promise of immediate pardon for repentance.
rows.anchor: و { اليوم يغفر الله لكم } بشارة بعاجل غفران الله ، لما تجدد يومئذ من توبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the conquest, Muḥammad asked Quraysh what they expected him to do; after they answered, he said he would speak Joseph's words, No reproach upon you today.
rows.anchor: فقال : أقول ما قال أخي يوسف : لا تثريب عليكم اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Abu Sufyan came to embrace Islam, al-ʿAbbās told him to recite Joseph's pardon; the Prophet prayed that God forgive him and his teacher.
rows.anchor: أن أبا سفيان لما جاء ليسلم قال له العباس : إذا أتيت الرسول فاتل عليه { لا تثريب عليكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers felt ashamed to accept Joseph's daily hospitality; he said their kinship and descent from Abraham made them honored in Egyptian eyes.
rows.anchor: إنك تدعونا إلى طعامك بكرة وعشية ، ونحن نستحي منك لما فرط منا فيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph said the Egyptians saw his brothers through their first impression, but their kinship with him and descent from Abraham had raised them in people's eyes.
rows.anchor: ولقد شرفت الآن بكم وعظمت في العيون حيث علم الناس أنكم إخوتي . وأني من حفدة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Joseph's shirt was inherited, kept as his amulet, and came from Paradise; Gabriel told him to send it because its fragrance would cure the afflicted and sick.
rows.anchor: هو القميص المتوارث الذي كان في تعويذ يوسف وكان من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yāti baṣīran may mean the father becomes sighted, supported by 12:96, or comes to Joseph already seeing, supported by the request to bring the whole family.
rows.anchor: يصر بصيرا ، كقولك : جاء البناء محكما ، بمعنى صار . ويشهد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Judah carried the shirt to make up for bringing Joseph's bloodied shirt and grieving Jacob; another report says he walked barefoot and bareheaded from Egypt to Canaan, eighty farsakhs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يهوذا هو الحامل ، قال : أنا أحزنته بحمل القميص ملطوخا بالدم إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caravan separated from Egypt's outskirts and passed its walls; Ibn ʿAbbās reads fa-lammā infaṣala al-ʿīr, when the caravan departed.
rows.anchor: خرجت من عريش مصر ، يقال : فصل من البلد فصولا ، إذا انفصل منه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the phrase as when the caravan separated and departed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس : ( فلما انفصل العير )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enabled Jacob to smell Joseph's shirt as it approached from a journey of eight days; he speaks to his grandchildren and those around him.
rows.anchor: أوجده الله ريح القميص حين أقبل من مسيرة ثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tufannidūn means accusing someone of senility or impaired reason; only a man is called mufannad because he had judgment in youth to lose in old age.
rows.anchor: والتفنيد : النسبة إلى الفند ، وهو الخرف وإنكار العقل من هرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob means that without their calling him senile, they would believe his report; their old error was excessive love, constant mention, and hope of reunion with Joseph, whom they thought dead.
rows.anchor: لفى ذهابك عن الصواب قدما في إفراط محبتك ليوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger or Jacob himself may have laid the shirt on Jacob's face; irtadda baṣīran means he returned to sight.
rows.anchor: ألقاه } طرح البشير القميص على وجه يعقوب . أو ألقاه يعقوب { فارتد بصيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alam aqul lakum may refer to Jacob's statement that he smelled Joseph or his command not to despair of God's relief; his following statement may begin a new sentence or quote his earlier words.
rows.anchor: كلام مبتدأ لم يقع عليه القول ، ولك أن توقعه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked how Joseph was, the messenger said he was Egypt's king; Jacob asked what use kingship was and what faith he had left, and rejoiced when told he was Muslim.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنه سأل البشير كيف يوسف ؟ فقال : هو ملك مصر : فقال : ما أصنع بالملك ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat that the messengers and believers must leave or return to the community's religion means one of those outcomes would necessarily occur; ʿādū can mean became, not that they had once been unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولكن العود بمعنى الصيرورة ، وهو كثير في كلام العرب كثرة فاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat may address each messenger and believer collectively, using the plural for the singular.
rows.anchor: أو خاطبوا به كل رسول ومن آمن به ، فغلبوا في الخطاب الجماعة على الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads the verbs for destroying the wrongdoers and settling the believers in the land in the third person, following the form of the preceding verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة : ( ليهلكن ) ، ( وليسكننكم ) بالياء اعتبارا لأوحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land inherited is the oppressors' land and homes, as in other verses about the inheritance of lands once held by wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأرض . أرض الظالمين وديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever harms his neighbor will inherit the neighbor's home; the author recounts a local oppressor's estate passing to him and recalls the report.
rows.anchor: من آذى جاره ورثه الله داره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative points to God's destruction of oppressors and settlement of believers in their lands; this is promised to those who fear His judgment or fear His oversight of their deeds.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما قضى به الله من إهلاك الظالمين وإسكان المؤمنين ديارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istaffataḥū may mean seeking God's victory against enemies, as in 8:19, or asking God to judge between parties, as in 7:89; a reading uses the imperative.
rows.anchor: واستنصروا الله على أعدائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may coordinate with God's revelation, or with His statement that He would destroy the wrongdoers, construing both as things He told the messengers.
rows.anchor: وهو معطوف على { أوحى * إليهم } وقرىء : ( واستفتحوا ) بلفظ الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers and believers prevailed while the arrogant opponents failed; alternatively, the unbelievers sought victory against the messengers, thinking themselves right, but failed.
rows.anchor: وقيل : واستفتح الكفار على الرسل ، ظنا منهم بأنهم على الحق والرسل على الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min warāʾihi means before him; the author cites a verse using warāʾ for what lies ahead as evidence.
rows.anchor: من ورائه } من بين يديه . قال : عسى الكرب الذي أمسيت فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell may be ahead of the damned in worldly life as they await it, or in the afterlife as they are raised and brought to it.
rows.anchor: وهذا وصف حاله وهو في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about being given pus coordinates with an omitted description of what happens in Hell, singling out one of its severest torments.
rows.anchor: قلت : على محذوف تقديره : من ورائه جهنم يلقى فيها ما يلقى ويسقي من ماء صديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadīd is an explanatory apposition to water, clarifying that it is fluid draining from the skin of Hell's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: قلت : صديد عطف بيان لماء ، قال : { ويسقى من ماء } فأبهمه إبهاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yataj arrʿuhu means he forces himself to swallow; kāda intensifies the phrase to mean he scarcely approaches being able to swallow it, linking to 24:40.
rows.anchor: دخل كاد للمبالغة . يعني : ولا يقارب أن يسيغه ، فكيف تكون الإساغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death's approach from every direction means all forms and causes of death surround him; alternatively, it reaches every part of his body, even a toe or every hair root.
rows.anchor: كأن أسباب الموت وأصنافه كلها قد تألبت عليه

rows.speaker: الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl says the continuing thick punishment is the severing and trapping of breaths inside bodies.
rows.anchor: وعن الفضيل : هو قطع الأنفاس وحبسها في الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that Meccans sought rain during a drought after the Prophet's prayer but were disappointed; the passage then shifts from the messengers' story to their failed request, replacing rain with Hell's pus.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون أهل مكة قد استفتحوا أي استمطروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bad attribute assigned to God is the people's need for sons, dislike of daughters, burying daughters from fear of poverty, and admission of extreme miserliness; God's highest attribute is self-sufficiency, transcendence, and generosity.
rows.anchor: وهي الحاجة إلى الأولاد الذكور وكرهة الإناث ووأدهن خشية الإملاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance and mercy coordinate with the place of li-tubayyina but are accusative purposes because they are acts of the one who sent the Book; the lam marks the addressee's action.
rows.anchor: وهدى * رحمة } معطوفان على محل { لتبين } إلا أنهما انتصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A purposive object must describe an act done by the agent of the related action.
rows.anchor: وإنما ينتصب مفعولا له ما كان فعل فاعل الفعل المعل .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the disputed matters were resurrection, which some believed including ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and practices of prohibition, denial, and affirmation.
rows.anchor: والذي اختلفوا فيه : البعث ؛ لأنه كان فيهم من يؤمن به ، ومنهم عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Listeners are those who hear with fairness and reflection; one who does not hear with the heart is like a deaf person.
rows.anchor: { لقوم يسمعون } سماع إنصاف وتدبر ؛ لأن من لم يسمع بقلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats al-anʿām as an indeclinable-looking plural in the form of a singular; this explains its masculine singular pronoun, unlike the feminine plural in 23:21.
rows.anchor: ذكر سيبويه الأنعام في باب ما لا ينصرف في الأسماء المفردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-anʿām may be a broken plural of naʿam or a singular collective with plural meaning; it can take a masculine singular pronoun or feminine agreement according to the intended sense.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يقال في الأنعام وجهان ، أحدهما : أن يكون تكسير نعم كأجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line uses naʿam with masculine singular agreement to illustrate the collective noun's grammatical behavior.
rows.anchor: في كل عام نعم تحوونه … يلقحه قوم وتنتجونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasqīkum is read with either fatḥa or ḍamma as a fresh statement answering how the lesson is seen.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( نسقيكم ) بالفتح والضم ، وهو استئناف ، كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates milk between dung and blood, with a barrier of divine power preventing either from affecting its color, taste, or smell.
rows.anchor: يخلق الله اللبن وسيطا بين الفرث والدم يكتنفانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account describes the animal's digestion as dung below, milk in the middle, and blood above; the liver sends each substance to its proper destination.
rows.anchor: فكان أسفله فرثا ، وأوسطه لبنا ، وأعلاه دما . والكبد مسلطة

rows.speaker: شقيق
rows.claim: Shuqayq defines sincerity as separating action from flaws, just as milk is separated from dung and blood.
rows.anchor: وسئل شقيق عن الإخلاص فقال : تمييز العمل من العيوب ، كتمييز اللبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʾigh means easy to pass through the throat; he says no one has ever choked on milk.
rows.anchor: { سآئغا } سهل المرور في الحلق ويقال : لم يغص أحد باللبن قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read sayghan with a doubled or light consonant, on the pattern of hayyin and layyin.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( سيغا ) ، بالتشديد . و ( سيغا ) ، بالتخفيف . كهين ولين .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first min is partitive, since milk is part of the livestock's contents; the second marks the starting point between dung and blood, or modifies milk as an earlier circumstantial phrase.
rows.anchor: لأن اللبن بعض ما في يطونها ، كقولك : أخذت من مال زيد ثوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some who hold semen pure argue that its passage through the urinary tract does not make it impure, just as pure milk emerges between dung and blood.
rows.anchor: وقد احتج بعض من يرى أن المني طاهر على من جعله نجسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fruit phrase may depend on an omitted we give you drink, be governed by you make, repeat a preposition for emphasis, or describe an omitted noun meaning fruit from which you make drink and provision.
rows.anchor: قلت : بمحذوف تقديره : ونسقيكم من ثمرات النخيل والأعناب ، أي : من عصيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If minhu is a repeated prepositional phrase, its pronoun refers to the omitted juice, as a pronoun may refer to an omitted noun elsewhere.
rows.anchor: إلى المضاف المحذوف الذي هو العصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukr means wine and is derived from the verbal noun for becoming intoxicated; the author cites a poem using the word.
rows.anchor: والسكر : الخمر ، سميت بالمصدر من سكر سكرا وسكرا . نحو رشد رشدا ورشدا

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and al-Nakhaʿī are among those who hold that this verse was abrogated.
rows.anchor: وممن قال بنسخها : الشعبي والنخعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is to combine the verse's reproach with its expression of divine favor.
rows.anchor: والثاني : أن يجمع بين العتاب والمنة . وقيل : السكر النبيذ

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa's view takes sukr as fermented nabīdh made from grape, raisin, or date juice, permissible until it intoxicates; he adduces this verse and a report.
rows.anchor: وهو حلال عند أبي حنيفة إلى حد السكر ويحتج بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī wrote books permitting nabīdh but declined to drink it in old age, saying consumption seemed indecent and unbecoming of good character.
rows.anchor: ولقد صنف شيخنا أبو علي الجبائي قدس الله روحه غير كتاب في تحليل النبيذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other readings take sukr to mean taste, or something like wine through indulging in people's reputations; good provision includes vinegar, syrup, dates, raisins, and similar foods.
rows.anchor: وقيل : السكر الطعم وأنشد : جعلت أعراض الكرام سكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukr itself may be construed as good provision, with the phrase meaning that people make from fruit both intoxicant and wholesome provision.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يجعل السكر رزقا حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If someone turns away from relatives, the needy, or travelers because ashamed to refuse them, they should still receive a response and not be left unanswered.
rows.anchor: فلا تتركهم غير مجابين إذا سألوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet would turn away and remain silent out of shyness when asked for something he did not have.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سئل شيئا وليس عنده أعرض عن السائل وسكت حياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtighāʾa raḥmatin may modify the conditional response: speak gently and promise well, seeking God's mercy by showing mercy and soothing hearts.
rows.anchor: فقل لهم قولا سهلا لينا وعدهم وعدا جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it modifies the condition: the person turns away because provision is lacking while seeking God's expected mercy; seeking stands for the preceding lack that caused it.
rows.anchor: وإن أعرضت عنهم لفقد رزق من ربك ترجو أن يفتح لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away may figuratively mean being unable to relieve their need, since a person who refuses to give often turns their face away.
rows.anchor: وإن لم تنفعهم ولم ترفع خصاصتهم لعدم الاستطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qawlan maysūran means easy, gentle speech; alternatively it is a prayer that God provide for both speaker and needy person and ease their poverty.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه : فقل لهم رزقنا الله وإياكم من فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's grief at their rejection is likened to a person abandoned by beloved companions who collapses in grief and destroys himself from longing.
rows.anchor: برجل فارقه أحبته وأعزته فهو يتساقط حسرات على آثارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bākhiʿ nafsaka is read in its original form or as an annexed phrase, meaning one who kills or destroys himself.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( باخع نفسك ) ، على الأصل ، وعلى الإضافة : أي قاتلها ومهلكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is future with the conditional reading in lam yuʾminū, but past with an yuʾminū understood causally as because they did not believe.
rows.anchor: وهو للاستقبال فيمن قرأ ( إن لم يؤمنوا ) وللمضي فيمن قرأ ( أن لم يؤمنوا ) بمعنى : لأن لم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asafan may be a causal object expressing excessive grief or anger, or a circumstantial description; asaf and asīf denote intense sorrow.
rows.anchor: { أسفا } مفعول له ، أي : لفرط الحزن . ويجوز أن يكون حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's adornment comprises worldly luxuries and pleasing things made for earth and its inhabitants; the test asks who acts best, with the best action being detachment rather than delusion by them.
rows.anchor: ما يصلح أن يكون زينة لها ولأهلها من زخارف الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will turn the earth's adornment into barren white land, removing its beauty as animals die and vegetation dries.
rows.anchor: بعد أن كانت خضراء معشبة ، في إزالة بهجته ، وإماطة حسنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's decoration and erasure are universal signs: God first creates countless kinds above it and then removes them as though they had never been.
rows.anchor: ذكر من الآيات الكلية تزيين الأرض مما خلق فوقها من الأجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave is a broad cave in a mountain; al-Raqīm is the sleepers' dog.
rows.anchor: والكهف : الغار الواسع في الجبل { والرقيم } اسم كلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other identifications of al-Raqīm are a lead tablet inscribed with their names at the cave, an inscription carved into the mountain, the valley, mountain, town, or their location between Ghaḍbān and Aylah.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو لوح من رصاص رقمت فيه أسماؤهم جعل على باب الكهف . وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kānū ʿajaban describes them as a marvel using a verbal noun, or means they were something possessing marvel.
rows.anchor: كانوا } آية { عجبا } من آياتنا وصفا بالمصدر ، أو على : ذات عجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested mercy is from God's stores: forgiveness, provision, and safety from enemies; preparing their affair means guiding them as they leave unbelievers or setting their whole affair right.
rows.anchor: من خزائن رحمتك ، وهي المغفرة والرزق والأمن من الأعداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God placed a barrier over their hearing, putting them into deep sleep in which sounds could not awaken them; the object, a covering, is omitted.
rows.anchor: ضربنا عليها حجابا من أن تسمع ، يعني : أنمناهم إنامة ثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinīna ʿadadan could mean many years or few, since many are enumerable; al-Zajjāj says a small number is known without counting, while a large number requires counting.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يريد الكثرة وأن يريد القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ay carries an interrogative sense that suspends the verb la-naʿlama; in the reading li-yaʿlama it is likewise suspended because the subject is the proposition, not an object governed by the verb.
rows.anchor: يتضمن معنى الاستفهام ، فعلق عنه { لنعلم } فلم يعمل فيه . وقرىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two parties may be the sleepers who disagreed after waking about their time asleep, as narrated in 18:19, or two outside groups who disputed it.
rows.anchor: المختلفين منهم في مدة لبثهم ؛ لأنهم لما انتبهوا اختلفوا في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥṣā is a past verb meaning which party counted or determined the duration of their stay.
rows.anchor: فعل ماض أي أيهم ضبط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading aḥṣā as a comparative is unsound: comparative formation from a non-triliteral verb is irregular, it cannot govern amadan, and an ellipsis to rescue it is contrived.
rows.anchor: ليس بالوجه السديد ، وذلك أن بناءه من غير الثلاثي المجرد ليس بقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not seek to learn something unknown; He intended the truth about the duration to become manifest when the sleepers awoke, increasing faith and reflection, helping believers, and serving as a clear sign to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وإنما أراد ما تعلق به العلم من ظهور الأمر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increased their guidance through granting success and steadfastness.
rows.anchor: بالتوفيق والتثبيت { وربطنا على قلوبهم } وقويناها بالصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthened their hearts to endure leaving home and comfort, flee with their faith, and publicly speak the truth.
rows.anchor: وقويناها بالصبر على هجر الأوطان والنعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They stood before the tyrant Diqyānūs without fear when he reproached them for abandoning idol worship.
rows.anchor: { إذ قاموا } بين يدي الجبار وهو دقيانوس ، من غير مبالاة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shataṭan is an excessively wrongful and extreme statement, from a root meaning to go far away.
rows.anchor: وهو الإفراط في الظلم والإبعاد فيه ، من شط : إذا بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāʾulāʾi is the subject, qawmunā an appositive, and ittakhadhū the predicate, phrased as a report that functions as a rejection.
rows.anchor: { هؤلاء } مبتدأ ، و { قومنا } عطف بيان { واتخذوا } خبر وهو إخبار في معنى إنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths challenge their people to produce proof for worshipping idols; this is a rebuke because proof is impossible, refutes blind imitation, and establishes that religion requires evidence.
rows.anchor: { بسلطان بين } وهو تبكيت ؛ لأن الإتيان بالسلطان على عبادة الأوثان محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascribing a partner to God is fabricating a lie against Him.
rows.anchor: بنسبة الشريك إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths' words are one another's speech after their resolve to flee with their religion; wa-mā yaʿbudūn is coordinated with the attached pronoun, meaning they left their people and their objects of worship.
rows.anchor: { وإذ اعتزلتموهم } خطاب من بعضهم لبعض ، حين صممت عزيمتهم على الفرار بدينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for God may be connected, since they acknowledged the Creator while associating others as Meccans did, or disconnected; alternatively, God interjects that the youths worshipped none but Him.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون استثناء متصلا ، على ما روي : أنهم كانوا يقرون بالخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marfiqan is read with fatḥa or kasra on the mīm and means something beneficial to rely upon.
rows.anchor: { مرفقا } قرىء ( بفتح الميم وكسرها ) وهو ما يرتفق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confidence in finding relief may express trust and strong hope in God, or come from a prophet who told them, or from one of the youths being a prophet.
rows.anchor: إما أن يقولوا ذلك ثقة بفضل الله وقوة في رجائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazāwar means to incline away; it comes from tatazāwar, with the initial tāʾ assimilated into zāy or deleted, and other readings retain or reshape the form.
rows.anchor: أصله تتزاور فخفف بإدغام التاء في الزاي أو حذفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings tazwar and tazwār also come from zawr, inclination; zawr can mean deviation from truth.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( تزور وتزوار ) بوزن تحمر وتحمار ، وكلها من الزور وهو الميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhāta al-yamīn means the direction called the right side.
rows.anchor: { ذات اليمين } جهة اليمين وحقيقتها . الجهة المسماة باليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqriḍuhum means cut away from or avoid them; a line by Dhū al-Rumma uses the verb for cutting across.
rows.anchor: تقطعهم لا تقربهم من معنى القطيعة والصرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They remain in shade throughout the day although the open space would expose them to sun; God shields them. Alternatively, the open area lets cool air reach them.
rows.anchor: أنهم في ظل نهارهم كله لا تصيبهم الشمس في طلوعها ولا غروبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sun-protected location is a special sign of divine honor; alternatively, their whole story is a sign, and the cave entrance faced north toward Banāt Naʿsh.
rows.anchor: اختصاصا لهم بالكرامة . وقيل : باب الكهف شمالي مستقبل لبنات نعش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse praises the youths for striving and surrendering to God: He guided and aided them to attain this rare honor and great sign; the abandoned person has no guide after God leaves him.
rows.anchor: ثناء عليهم بأنهم جاهدوا في الله وأسلموا له وجوههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taḥsabuhum is read with either vowel on the sīn and addresses any observer; yaqiz means awake. Their open eyes, frequent turning, or turning once or twice yearly may make them appear awake.
rows.anchor: قيل : عيونهم مفتحة وهم نيام ، فيحسبهم الناظر لذلك أيقاظا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sleepers are read as being turned by God, or their turning is read as a verbal noun governed by an implied verb.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ويقلبهم ) بالياء والضمير لله تعالى . وقرىء ( وتقلبهم ) على المصدر منصوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has kālibuhum, meaning the companion of their dog, rather than their dog.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جعفر الصادق ( وكالبهم ) أي وصاحب كلبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bāsiṭ dhirāʿayhi depicts a past scene; the active participle's annexation is genuinely definite only if the past is narrated as present.
rows.anchor: { باسط ذراعيه } حكاية حال ماضية ؛ لأن اسم الفاعل لا يعمل إذا كان في معنى المضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Waṣīd means the courtyard, threshold, or door; a cited poem witnesses its use for a threshold.
rows.anchor: الوصيد : الفناء ، وقيل : العتبة . وقيل : الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-muliʾat is read with a doubled lām for emphasis; the hamza may be eased and changed to yāʾ, and ruʿban is read light or heavy.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( ولملئت ) بتشديد اللام للمبالغة . وقرىء ( بتخفيف الهمزة وقلبها ياء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their terrifying appearance may come from divine awe, long nails and hair and huge bodies, or the desolation of the place.
rows.anchor: وذلك لما ألبسهم الله من الهيبة . وقيل : لطول أظفارهم وشعورهم وعظم أجرامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: During a Roman campaign, Muʿāwiya wanted to view the sleepers; Ibn ʿAbbās said God had barred someone better than him, but Muʿāwiya sent men who were burned by a wind in the cave.
rows.anchor: فلما دخلوا الكهف بعث الله عليهم ريحا فأحرقتهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās told Muʿāwiya that he had no right to uncover the sleepers, since God had prevented someone better than him from doing so.
rows.anchor: قد منع الله تعالى منه من هو خير منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading of law iṭṭalaʿta has ḍamma on the wāw.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( لو اطلعت ) ، بضم الواو .
